full_judgment: 10. We have looked into the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act, 1950). We have found no provision therein which authorised the Ministry/the Government through any Ministry to direct the Revenue Officer to accept rent from a particular person. From the impugned judgment, it appears that the High Court Division failed to give its attention to this legal aspect of the case. Procedures as to the maintenance and revisions of the record of rights have been laid down in Chapter XVII of the Act, 1950 and the Rules framed thereunder vide State Acquisition Rules, 1955 and as per the provisions incorporated therein, one has to apply to the concerned Revenue Officer for mutation of his/its name and if such prayer is allowed then and then only the question of accepting rent from that person would arise, but in the instant case, it does not appear that writ-respondent No.6 or anyone on its behalf ever filed any application to the concerned authority for mutation of its name or record its name in the record of rights and accept rent. Therefore, the impugned Memo issued by the Ministry of Land was passed without any sanction of law and as such, the same cannot be sustained. However, we are of the view that writ respondent No.6 if so advised, may file proper application before the appropriate authority to mutate or record its name and if such application is filed, the concerned authority shall consider the same in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Act, 1950 and the rules of the State Acquisition Rules, 1955 and any party including the writ-petitioners shall have the opportunity to raise legal objection, if any, and the concerned authority shall decide the matter on the basis of the materials produced before it,
